headline: Crude bomb explodes in front of Supreme Court
summary: The blast occurred shortly after the International Crimes Tribunal-2 sentenced seven Awami League leaders to death.
details: A crude bomb exploded in front of the Supreme Court in Dhaka this afternoon around 1:15 pm, according to Shahbagh Police Station Inspector (Operations) Mainul Islam.
The explosion took place approximately one hour after the International Crimes Tribunal-2 delivered a significant verdict.
The tribunal sentenced Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six others to death in a crimes against humanity case.
The case pertains to atrocities committed during the July Uprising in 2024.
Other convicts include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, and Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash.
The list of those sentenced to death also includes Jubo League General Secretary Moinul Hossain Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain, and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Enan.
Police are currently working to identify the individuals responsible for detonating the cocktail.
caption:
A crude bomb blast hits the Supreme Court entrance shortly after a major death sentence verdict.

A crude bomb exploded in front of the Supreme Court in Dhaka this afternoon around 1:15 pm, according to Shahbagh Police Station Inspector (Operations) Mainul Islam.

The explosion took place approximately one hour after the International Crimes Tribunal-2 delivered a significant verdict.

The tribunal sentenced Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six others to death in a crimes against humanity case.

The case pertains to atrocities committed during the July Uprising in 2024.

Other convicts include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, and Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash.

The list of those sentenced to death also includes Jubo League General Secretary Moinul Hossain Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain, and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Enan.

Police are currently working to identify the individuals responsible for detonating the cocktail.

headline: Moody's revises Bangladesh outlook to stable from negative
summary: The global ratings agency cites eased political pressures and improved external positions as key drivers for the upgrade in outlook.
details: Global ratings agency Moody's has revised its outlook for Bangladesh to stable from negative, maintaining the long-term rating at B2.
The agency stated that acute political and external pressures that previously drove the negative outlook have eased, leaving risks more balanced at the current rating level.
Moody's highlighted that the post-election transition and a strong governing mandate have reduced the risk of political uncertainty derailing necessary reforms.
The country's external position has improved due to rebuilt foreign exchange reserves, record remittances, and a more flexible exchange rate regime.
Continued engagement with the IMF and other international financial institutions is seen as an important anchor for external financing and reform.

This revision comes after S&P Global and Fitch Ratings both revised their outlooks for Bangladesh to negative in June and May respectively, citing banking sector weakness and macroeconomic vulnerabilities.
